standard.title: Clauses with subject-verb agreement
standard.description: understand that a clause is a unit of grammar usually containing a subject and a verb, and that subject-verb agreement is required
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand how compound sentences connect ideas using coordinating conjunctions (AC9E2LA06). They have not yet examined the internal structure of a clause — specifically the subject-verb relationship — or the agreement rule.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students understand that a clause contains a subject and a verb, and that subjects and verbs must agree in number.

nodes.label: Identifying clause elements
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the verb and subject in a clause.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the verb and subject in at least three clauses by locating the verb first, then finding what or who the verb is about.
nodes.typical_width: Identify clauses by locating verbs and the key words that link to the verbs; practise identifying subjects and verbs across different sentence types and text contexts.
wider: Find clauses in different text types (narrative, information, instruction) and compare how subjects vary — from simple nouns to noun groups
Explore what happens to a clause when the subject is removed — discussing why subjects are necessary for meaning
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot reliably identify the subject and verb in a clause cannot apply subject-verb agreement rules at N2 — agreement requires knowing which subject the verb must match.

response_modes.reason: Clause identification is a precision skill — knowing the definition doesn't translate automatically into reliable identification. Students need repeated practice across varied examples before subject and verb identification becomes fluent.

success_criteria: Student correctly identifies the verb in a clause
Student correctly identifies the subject that goes with that verb

nodes.label: Subject-verb agreement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify when a singular subject requires a singular verb form and a plural subject requires a plural verb form.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two examples of subject-verb agreement (one singular, one plural) and explain why the verb form matches the subject.
nodes.typical_width: Understand and apply subject-verb agreement: singular subjects take singular verbs, plural subjects take plural verbs — recognise and correct agreement errors.
wider: Identify tricky agreement cases (e.g. collective nouns, compound subjects) and discuss why they are harder to get right
Find subject-verb agreement errors in student-level writing samples and explain the correction

response_modes.reason: Subject-verb agreement errors are common in student writing and persist without targeted practice. This is a precision skill that requires repeated application across varied sentence types, not just comprehension of the rule.

success_criteria: Student identifies whether a subject is singular or plural
Student selects or confirms the correct verb form to match the subject
